Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Member: Taylor Foster  
Member ID: W684120124  
Plan: Aetna Commercial/ACA — Rhode Island  
Reference number: POC-157F6EFE74-80557  
Requested service: Lumbar disc surgery/decompression  
CPT: 63030  
Denial date: August 23, 2026

Dear Aetna Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal Aetna’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lumbar decompression/discectomy. The denial states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. Based on the clinical records submitted with the authorization request, the procedure is medically necessary and satisfies the relevant criteria in Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin No. 0743, Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion.

The applicable Aetna policy states:

“Lumbar laminectomy for individuals with a herniated disc when all of the following criteria are met:”

“Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated;”

“Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings;”

“Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy Footnote1 * (unless there are indications for waiver of requirements for conservative management);” and

“Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression;”

The records address each of these requirements:

1. Herniated disc and corresponding compression  
The lumbar MRI dated July 15, 2026, shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing right L5 nerve root. This is objective imaging evidence of a herniated disc, severe stenosis, and nerve-root compression at the level being treated.

2. Symptoms of neural compression  
I have radicular pain extending into the right calf, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the L4-L5/L5 imaging findings. These findings establish symptoms and examination abnormalities consistent with compression of the affected nerve root.

3. Failure of conservative treatment  
Symptoms have continued and progressed for approximately 12 months despite extensive conservative treatment. This includes:

- Supervised physical therapy focused on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility for 14 weeks, from April 3, 2026, through July 10, 2026;
- Twenty-four completed physical-therapy visits, documented in the physical-therapy discharge note;
- NSAID treatment for four months without adequate relief; and
- A corticosteroid injection on May 19, 2026, which provided only three weeks of partial relief.

This treatment substantially exceeds six weeks of conservative care and did not adequately control the symptoms.

4. Functional limitation  
I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes because of the lower-back and radicular symptoms. The symptoms interfere substantially with ordinary daily activities and functional mobility.

5. Persistent and progressive condition  
The pain has continued for 12 months and has progressed despite treatment. Rest has not relieved the symptoms. The MRI-confirmed severe lateral recess stenosis and L5 nerve-root compression provide an anatomic explanation for the persistent radicular pain, examination findings, neurologic deficit, and functional limitation.

The records also do not identify an apparent contraindication to the requested treatment. There is no active infection or untreated substance use; BMI is 29; and I am a non-smoker.

For these reasons, I request that Aetna overturn the denial and authorize CPT 63030 at the L4-L5 level. Please have the request reviewed by an appropriate physician specializing in spinal surgery or neurosurgery who was not involved in the original denial.

If Aetna maintains the denial, please provide the complete case-specific medical-necessity rationale, the clinical criteria and policy version applied to this request, the effective or revision date of that version, the records relied upon, and an explanation identifying which specific criterion Aetna believes has not been met.

Please include this letter and all enclosed records in the appeal file and send the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Taylor Foster  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]
